business_problem: AdventHealth needed to reduce administrative and documentation burden across clinical and operational teams so staff could handle more demand without sacrificing quality or clinician time with patients.
solution_summary: AdventHealth approached AI rollout as an adoption problem rather than a pilot problem, using ChatGPT Enterprise and later ChatGPT for Healthcare to redesign workflows across a large health system. Early work focused on utilization management, where physician advisors spend significant time reviewing charts, checking criteria, and drafting rationales; with ChatGPT for Healthcare, the system can generate structured summaries, highlight relevant details, and draft first-pass rationales while clinicians retain final responsibility. The organization measures these improvements with timestamps in electronic health records and other process-native throughput data instead of relying on anecdotal feedback. Similar patterns now apply beyond clinical roles: drafting documents, converting policies into structured formats, summarizing notes, and accelerating internal workflows across finance, HR, and IT. Governance, privacy, and peer-based adoption groups remain central so AI becomes a trusted source of “time back” that can be reinvested into patient care and higher-value work.

solution_components.name: ChatGPT Enterprise
solution_components.role: Supports enterprise-scale drafting, summarization, and workflow redesign across non-clinical functions.

solution_components.name: ChatGPT for Healthcare
solution_components.role: Generates structured clinical summaries and draft rationales in regulated care workflows.

data_flow: Clinical charts, internal documents, policies, and notes flow into ChatGPT workspaces to generate structured summaries, rationales, and first drafts. System-level timestamps and throughput data are then used to measure the impact and verify whether reclaimed time is translating into operational capacity.
business_outcome: AdventHealth reduced time spent on repetitive tasks, expanded clinical and operational capacity without additional staffing, and gave clinicians and staff more time to focus on patients and higher-value work.
metrics: 80% reduction in time spent on administrative tasks
A 10-minute task can be reduced to about 2 minutes in some workflows
architecture_clues: Adoption is tracked as messages per user per business day
Peer groups share function-specific prompts and workflows instead of relying only on centralized training
Impact is measured through system-level timestamps in EHRs and workflow systems
Leaders frame AI as “time back” rather than automation
